abilities.name: Wrath of Hera
abilities.description: Lashes out at a structure. Costs divinity equal to the power; at power 2 it damages a target without setting it alight.

abilities.name: Tale of a Grievance
abilities.description: Tells the story of a wrong done to her, told aloud to everyone present and recorded as a legend.

lore.statement: Hera is the daughter of Cronus and Rhea, sister and wife of Zeus, and queen of the immortals, honored by all the gods on Olympus.
In Hesiod, Hera bears Hebe, Ares, and Eileithyia to Zeus; in the Iliad, the Eileithyiai, who send the pangs of childbirth, are called Hera's daughters.
Argos, Sparta, and Mycenae are the cities dearest to Hera.
Hera reproaches Zeus for deciding matters in secret, apart from her, and never being willing to tell her what he intends.

After Zeus bears Athena from his own head, Hera bears Hephaestus without union with Zeus and quarrels furiously with her husband (Hesiod); in the Hymn to Apollo she rages that Zeus bore Athena apart from her, prays for a child as strong as he, and bears the monster Typhaon.
Hera outwits Zeus: he falls asleep in her arms on Mount Ida, which he later calls her trick and deception, and she once tricked him into an oath that made Eurystheus, not Heracles, ruler.
Hera swears by Earth, Heaven, and the water of the Styx, the gravest oath of the gods, and by Zeus's head and their marriage bed.

Hera's wrath pursues Heracles, Zeus's son by Alcmene: the Iliad names her storm against him at sea and her wrath that brought him down; Apollodorus adds serpents sent to his cradle, madness, and the same storm after Troy.
Hera asks Zeus for the cow that Io has become and sets Argus to guard her; in Ovid's telling she relents and Io regains human form.
Hera's hostility to Zeus's Theban lover Semele ends in Semele's death when she asks to see Zeus as he really is.

variants.note: Hesiod and the Hymn to Hera make Rhea her mother without saying where she grew up. In the Iliad Hera says Ocean and Tethys reared her after Zeus cast Cronus down. This profile keeps Rhea as her mother and leaves her upbringing unstated.

The Iliad gives Hera's storm after Troy, her trick that delayed his birth in Eurystheus's favor, and her wrath at his death; Apollodorus adds serpents in the cradle and madness. The accounts pick different episodes, so whether they are one grudge is left open; this profile treats them as one long grudge.

inventions.statement: Hera's domain troubles are the game's own.
inventions.reason: A roof that leaks onto stores, and damp that spoils household cloth or food, are troubles the game draws on a season's odds and a floor, taking goods. Hera's claim to weather is weak in the sources, so the game gives her the household instead; the cited line is adapted, not quoted, and no source tells these episodes.

inventions.statement: Hera's wrath is expressed in play as a damaging strike on structures, below the ignition threshold.
inventions.reason: The world has no action that harms a person or curses. Her myths aim her anger at people (Io, Semele, Heracles), not buildings, so this mapping is a game stand-in.

inventions.statement: Hera airs her grievances by telling tales that are recorded as legends.
inventions.reason: Legend is the world's only action that records speech or tale; it is a game mapping, not a mythic device.

inventions.statement: The drive weights and the starting disposition toward Zeus are authored tuning.
inventions.reason: The sources describe temperament in prose; the numbers are a design choice to be revised against play.

troubles.statement: A leaking roof spoils a household's stores. Autumn and winter.
Damp spoils household cloth or food. Winter.
